knowledge_gaps: Averaging 32 uniformly sampled pairwise logistic terms has the same expected objective as using one negative under the same sampling distribution. It can reduce gradient variance, but does not inherently emphasize hard competitors. Stronger discrimination and the potential rating of 8 are therefore insufficiently supported.

The proposal changes terminal masking, endpoint recency, negative count, and possibly the baseline loss simultaneously. Without controlled ablations, any improvement cannot be attributed to a specific change. The report also lacks a trial and runtime allocation within the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget.

Reproduction requires the exact endpoint probability distribution, eligible endpoint range, context truncation reserving one mask slot, negative replacement policy, empty-pool handling, and loss weighting between terminal examples and random-mask examples. Averaging targets within each example versus globally produces different weights.

Baseline validation HR@10 and checkpoint-selection details are absent. With 200 validation users per category, small gains and repeated selection on the same users need cautious interpretation. Training margins must use a fixed diagnostic protocol and cannot establish improved compatibility or current-intent alignment.

Originality 3 is reasonable, but difficulty 3 is provisional without the supplied baseline implementation. The diagnostic adapter must retain B×L inputs despite multi-negative training, and all supervised targets must remain hidden under the task's stricter masking requirement.
